clusters.text: Greg Abbott ordered flags lowered to half-staff for the October 7 anniversary in solidarity with Israel.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The Governor's office press release, dated October 6, 2026, says Abbott ordered the U.S. and Texas flags at all state buildings lowered to half-staff on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, "in solidarity with the State of Israel."
 The order was issued on October 6, which matches the date the claim was first seen on X. 
His formal order to DPS Colonel Martin cites Chapter 3100 of the Texas Government Code.
 The order marks the third anniversary of the Hamas attack, and Abbott's statement says 
Hamas "murdered more than 1,200 men, women, and children."
 The Houston Chronicle, Dallas Express and Fox 44 report the same thing. The Chronicle adds that 
Abbott issued similar orders in October 2023 and 2024.
 The claim's wording, including the solidarity framing and the date, matches the official record.

clusters.event: YouGov Texas poll: Talarico 50-44, Hinojosa 48-47
clusters.text: A YouGov poll finds Hispanic Texans back James Talarico over Ken Paxton 61% to 34%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The YouGov poll ran Sept. 28–Oct. 5 and surveyed 3,625 Texas voters. 
It showed Talarico leading overall, 50%–44%.
 The blog Off the Kuff, summarizing YouGov's highlights, reports that 
Talarico leads 61-34 among Hispanic voters while trailing 55-39 among white voters.
 That matches the claim's pollster, candidates and 61–34 figures. I couldn't open YouGov's own release or crosstabs, so the Hispanic numbers rest on that secondary summary. Other pollsters show smaller Hispanic margins, for example 
Emerson at 54% to 39%
. Those are different polls and don't contradict the YouGov figure. The claim is also loosely worded: it says "Hispanic Texans" rather than Hispanic voters or likely voters.

clusters.event: YouGov Texas poll: Talarico 50-44, Hinojosa 48-47
clusters.text: A YouGov poll finds Hispanic Texans back Gina Hinojosa over Greg Abbott 58% to 37%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Newsweek reported on a YouGov poll of 3,622 likely Texas voters, fielded Sept. 28–Oct. 5. 
It had Hinojosa narrowly ahead of Abbott, 48% to 47%.
 Newsweek reported that 
Hinojosa leads Hispanic voters 58 percent to 37 percent
, and Wonderwall repeated the same crosstab figures. RealClearPolling's listing of the same YouGov poll (9/28–10/5, 3,622 LV) matches the topline. The claim's numbers, pollster and candidates all match. I did not see the YouGov release or crosstabs themselves, so the subgroup figure rests on secondary reporting. The claim is also easy to misread as a general result, but the 58–37 figure is a subgroup of likely voters in one poll. Other polls show smaller Hispanic margins: UMass Lowell/YouGov had 51–43 and UT had 56–42.

clusters.event: YouGov Texas poll: Talarico 50-44, Hinojosa 48-47
clusters.text: A YouGov poll of Texas likely voters has Gina Hinojosa at 48% and Greg Abbott at 47%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim matches the poll's reported numbers. 
Newsweek reports a YouGov poll of 3,622 likely voters, conducted September 28 through October 5, with Hinojosa narrowly ahead of Abbott, 48% to 47%, and 5% undecided.
 
RealClearPolling lists the same YouGov poll (9/28–10/5, 3,622 LV, margin of error 3.0).
 Its table shows Abbott at 47 and Hinojosa at 48. Fox 7 Austin also reports the 48–47 result. 
It describes the sample as 3,625 registered Texas voters.
 That is a small mismatch with the likely-voter label used by Newsweek and RealClearPolling. The result is within the margin of error, so the race is a statistical tie. The claim doesn't say otherwise, and it isn't misleading. Other YouGov-branded polls give different results, such as the UMass Lowell/YouGov poll with Abbott ahead 48–44. The claim doesn't point to either of those polls.

clusters.event: UMass Lowell/YouGov poll: Senate tied 45-45, Abbott 48-44
clusters.text: A UMass Lowell/YouGov poll has Greg Abbott leading Gina Hinojosa 48% to 44%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
UMass Lowell's own press release, dated 10/08/2026, reports 
Abbott with 48% support, compared with 44% for Democratic challenger state Rep. Gina Hinojosa
. The poll surveyed 850 likely voters and was 
fielded Sept. 18 through Sept. 28, with an adjusted margin of error of +/-4.5 points
. Political Wire and Newsweek report the same figures. Newsweek adds that Abbott's lead is within the margin of error. The claim states the pollster, the candidates and the numbers correctly. It leaves out that the fieldwork was in late September and that other polls, such as UT/YouGov and NYT/Siena, showed Hinojosa narrowly ahead. That context doesn't make the stated figure wrong.

clusters.text: Greg Abbott should debate Gina Hinojosa, and refusing means he does not deserve to be governor.

clusters.event: UMass Lowell/YouGov poll: Senate tied 45-45, Abbott 48-44
clusters.text: The UMass Lowell/YouGov poll has Ken Paxton and James Talarico tied at 45% in the Senate race.
clusters.verdict_basis: The claim is accurate as worded. Political Wire, Newsweek and Texas Politics all report that the UMass Lowell/YouGov poll, released Oct. 8, 2026, has Talarico and Paxton at 45% each among likely voters. Texas Politics adds that it surveyed 850 likely voters from Sept. 18–28, with a margin of error of ±4.5 points, 7% undecided and 2% for Libertarian Ted Brown. Fieldwork was in late September, so the poll is older than a separate YouGov poll from Oct. 6 that had Talarico ahead 50–44 (cited by AOL). That is a different poll, and the claim doesn't conflate the two. The claim's "Context: Gov. Abbott" tag doesn't affect it. The same UMass Lowell poll also covered the governor's race.

clusters.event: Oct 7 anniversary: Abbott orders flags to half-staff
clusters.text: JB Pritzker and the Democratic Governors Association are each giving $1 million to Gina Hinojosa's campaign.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The New York Times report, syndicated by GV Wire on Oct. 7, says 
Pritzker and the Democratic Governors Association are each sending $1 million to support her bid, Pritzker and a top DGA official said Tuesday
. The same report says 
the DGA's $1 million is the group's first investment in the state
. The Hill, Reason and The Week repeat the figure. The Week words it as "at least $1 million". A low-quality aggregator (eciks.org) cites CBS News as saying Pritzker's gift was $1.2 million. I found no primary CBS or campaign-finance record to confirm that. It would not contradict the claim anyway, since it is still at least $1 million. I did not find a Texas Ethics Commission filing showing the money received. The claim is therefore supported as a pledge or announcement by the donors themselves, not as a recorded receipt.

clusters.event: Oct 7 anniversary: Abbott orders flags to half-staff
clusters.text: Greg Abbott did not lower flags or mention the anniversary of the Uvalde shooting.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim doesn't say which anniversary it means, and the record differs by year.

- 2023 (first anniversary): 
The governor's own press release says Abbott ordered flags lowered statewide and called for a moment of silence on the one-year anniversary.
 The release also quotes him directly on the tragedy. So the claim is false for 2023.
- 2024 (second anniversary): 
Fox News reported that Abbott did not publicly acknowledge the anniversary, and the shooting was not mentioned on his social media accounts or in his office's press releases.
 That fits the claim for 2024. A 2023 AOL/Independent piece also described 
Abbott and Patrick as conspicuously silent on the anniversary morning
, but that outlet's account conflicts with the official release.
- 2025 and 2026: I found no primary record or news report showing what Abbott did on the third or fourth anniversaries. The only 2026 item I found is a 
Giffords statement from May 22, 2026
, which says nothing about Abbott. A Substack post from October 8, 2026 claims he has not marked the anniversary since 2023, but it is partisan and not a primary source.

A blanket "did not lower flags or mention the anniversary"

clusters.event: Oct 7 anniversary: Abbott orders flags to half-staff
clusters.text: Greg Abbott values Israeli children more than Texas children.
An eight-time Texas high school football state champion coach backs Gina Hinojosa.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim holds up. 
Former longtime Aledo football head coach Tim Buchanan, an eight-time state champion, gave a public endorsement to Gina Hinojosa in a video
, according to a Yahoo-syndicated report. The Houston Chronicle likewise reports that 
Hinojosa tapped former Aledo High School coach and athletic director Tim Buchanan for her ad "Coach"
, and that 
eight of Aledo's 12 state titles came under Buchanan's leadership
. The Hinojosa campaign's own press release and ad transcript, dated Oct. 9, 2026, have Buchanan saying 
he won eight state championships
 and that 
he voted for Abbott three times, but is getting off the sidelines for Gina Hinojosa
. One caveat: the endorsement comes through a paid campaign ad. Reporting calls it an endorsement and shows him backing her on camera, so the wording "backs" fits.

clusters.text: Gina Hinojosa will meet Greg Abbott at the Governor's Mansion next Thursday at 10 AM.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Hinojosa did post "Governor Abbott, I'll meet you at the Governor's Mansion next Thursday at 10 AM" on Oct. 8 (
her X post
). The date and time match: 
KSAT reported she called on him to meet her at the Mansion on Oct. 15 at 10 a.m.
 But this is a one-sided debate challenge, not a scheduled meeting. The Houston Chronicle reported that 
Abbott's campaign did not respond
 and that 
the appearance is unlikely to amount to more than another news conference
. As of Oct. 13, the Texarkana Gazette reported that 
Abbott, who debated his three previous Democratic opponents, has not agreed to a debate
. The claim, worded as a settled fact that Hinojosa "will meet Greg Abbott," implies a mutual engagement that no reporting shows. Only her own appearance and invitation are documented.

clusters.text: A canvasser for Greg Abbott was visibly upset when a homeowner said he would not support Abbott.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The only matching incident I found is from June 2022. In that case, an Abbott canvasser, Monique Dawson, was filmed on a Hurst, Texas doorbell camera. When homeowner James Whitfield said "Absolutely not" to supporting Abbott, 
she burst out laughing
, according to Yahoo/Newsweek. The Houston Chronicle and MySanAntonio likewise describe her as amused, not upset. Dawson herself said 
she saw "pure amusement"
 on Whitfield's face, and she then said "Everybody's gotta have a job." I found no 2026 reporting of a canvasser for Abbott being visibly upset at a homeowner's refusal. The claim's "visibly upset" detail is contradicted by the one documented case, and I couldn't tie it to any new, verifiable incident. If the X post is recirculating the 2022 clip, it misstates what the clip shows. If it refers to a different, new video, I couldn't find that.

clusters.event: YouGov Texas poll: Talarico 50-44, Hinojosa 48-47
clusters.text: The YouGov poll has James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 50% to 44%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
A YouGov poll of 3,625 voters, conducted Sept. 28–Oct. 5, found Talarico ahead of Paxton 50% to 44%. 
Fox 7 Austin reported the 50%–44% result and noted that 2% chose someone else, 3% were undecided and 1% would not vote.
 
RealClearPolling lists the same poll, with a 3.0-point margin of error.
 
Newsweek also reported it.
 The claim's numbers and attribution match. Two caveats: Fox 7 calls the sample registered voters while RealClearPolling and Newsweek call them likely voters, and a separate UMass Lowell/YouGov poll, fielded Sept. 18–28, 
had the two tied at 45% to 45%
. The claim's 50–44 figure belongs to the Sept. 28–Oct. 5 poll, so it is not wrong, but "the YouGov poll" is not the only YouGov poll of this race.

clusters.text: Greg Abbott allowed over 200 mosques to be built in Texas.
clusters.verdict_basis:
No record shows that Abbott "allowed" any mosques to be built, and the "over 200" figure doesn't match any count of mosques built during his tenure. Mosques are privately built under local zoning and permitting. The governor has no approval role. The cited counts are totals of existing mosques, not new construction. The ISPU/Faith Communities Today survey, as cited by Not the Bee, found 
Texas mosques grew from 166 to 224 between 2010 and 2020
. Online directories list 
332 mosques
, and texasmuslim.org gives 
roughly 280 to 340
. These totals include mosques that predate Abbott, who became governor in January 2015. A viral figure of about 48 new mosques in two years is, per Not the Bee, from an op-ed and is disputed. Abbott's documented actions point the other way: 
he launched investigations into the proposed EPIC City project
 and 
sent the East Plano Islamic Center a cease-and-desist letter over funeral services
. These are state actions against specific projects, not approval of mosque construction. The "200+" number appears to come from total counts, and the "allowed" framing gets his role wrong. I found no primary record, such as a state filing or a permit coun

clusters.event: Oct 7 anniversary: Abbott orders flags to half-staff
clusters.text: Gina Hinojosa will be able to crush Greg Abbott with this funding.
Under Greg Abbott, Texas has higher taxes and more data centers.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The data-center half is broadly supported. Trackers cited by Visual Capitalist and Electric Choice put Texas second to Virginia in facility count and first in the pipeline of planned sites. The Texas Tribune reports that 138 data centers now qualify for the state sales-tax exemption, with 59 certified in 2026 alone. The tax half has no stated baseline, and the available comparisons don't clearly support "higher taxes." The Tax Foundation figures republished by Ledgerism and PaycheckTaxCalculator put Texas's total state and local burden at 8.6% of income, below the 11.2% national average (46th highest). The Tax Foundation's 2026 competitiveness index ranks Texas 7th overall, and WalletHub finds Texas's property-tax burden ranks 9th highest. So property and sales taxes are relatively high, while there is no income tax and the overall burden is below average. The claim also leaves out that the data-center boom comes with a sales-tax break costing over $1 billion a year, which Abbott and his opponent Gina Hinojosa both want to end, according to the Houston Chronicle.

Because the claim doesn't say what Texas is being compared with, the tax statement is at best partly true. T

clusters.text: A UH/Hobby School poll of Harris County has Gina Hinojosa leading Greg Abbott 56% to 40%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The University of Houston Hobby School's October 2026 Harris County report says 
Hinojosa (56%) holds a 16-point lead over Abbott (40%) among likely Harris County voters
. Houston Public Media reported the same figures. It added that 
Libertarian Pat Dixon got 2% and 2% were unsure
. CW39 also reported the 56%–40% result. The claim's pollster, geography, candidates and numbers all match. The only thing it leaves out is that the sample is likely voters, which doesn't change what the claim says.

clusters.text: The UH/Hobby poll has James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 58% to 36% in Harris County.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The University of Houston Hobby School's Harris County report, fielded Oct. 3–8, 2026, says 
Talarico (58%) holds a 22 point lead over Republican Ken Paxton (36%) among likely Harris County voters.
 The Hobby School's project page repeats those figures. 
Among likely Harris County voters, Democrat James Talarico (58%) holds a 22 point lead over Republican Ken Paxton (36%).
 The Texan also reports the same numbers, from a survey of 2,750 likely voters. 
It found 58 percent for Talarico and 36 percent for Paxton, with 2 percent for Libertarian Ted Brown and 4 percent unsure.
 Houston Public Media and Style Magazine also report the 22-point lead. The claim is worded correctly: the poll is the UH Hobby School's, the numbers are right, and it is a Harris County result, not a statewide one.

clusters.event: YouGov Texas poll: Talarico 50-44, Hinojosa 48-47
clusters.text: Polling in the Texas governor's race is tightening.
clusters.verdict_basis:
By the Oct. 6 posting date, the trend toward a closer race was well documented. Newsweek said Abbott led by 7 points in a UT/Texas Politics Project poll in early June and by 6 in a late-July Texas Southern University poll. It also said 
no public poll since mid-September has shown him up by more than 5
. The NYT/Siena poll moved from 
Abbott 51–44 in June to Hinojosa 49–46 in late September
, and a YouGov poll had 
Hinojosa ahead 48–47
. The picture since then is mixed. Marist's Oct. 8–11 poll has 
Abbott 49%, Hinojosa 45% among likely voters
, and ReconMR has Abbott 
edging ahead after trailing by four in September
. RealClearPolling's average is 
Abbott +2.2
. So the race is much closer than in the summer, but it isn't narrowing in a straight line, and polls have 
traded leads all fall
.

clusters.event: Public First Action/Guidant polls (Texas Senate and governor)
clusters.text: A Public First Action/Guidant poll has Greg Abbott leading Gina Hinojosa 46% to 44%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
**Basis:** Political Wire reported on Oct. 7, 2026 that 
a Public First Action/Guidant poll of likely voters, with a ±3.46% margin of error, has Abbott leading Hinojosa 46% to 44%, with Dixon at 4%.
 Journalist Burgess Everett posted the same toplines on X, saying the poll was 
commissioned by Public First Action and conducted by Guidant
. So the numbers, the sponsor and the pollster all match the claim. The claim leaves out that this is a sponsor-commissioned poll, and Political Wire labels Guidant "(R)". It also leaves out that an earlier Guidant poll for the same group, 
fielded Sept. 20-28, showed Hinojosa ahead 46-42
. I couldn't find the original Public First Action release, so the evidence is secondary reporting. The 2-point gap is within the margin of error. I did not find a conflict over the figures themselves.

clusters.text: CNN's Harry Enten said Republicans have collapsed in Texas.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Harry Enten did discuss a large Democratic shift in Texas around October 12–13, 2026, but the reporting I found doesn't show him saying Republicans "collapsed." 
Enten said Republicans won the 2024 statewide House vote by 18 points, while current aggregate polling has Democrats ahead by 2. He called that a 20-point swing.
 
He also said the shift could cut Republican seat gains from mid-decade redistricting to between zero and two, down from up to five.
 He described it as 
"a very unusual pattern occurring in the great state of Texas"
 and said there was 
no clear leader in the statewide generic ballot polls
. A week earlier he had said Republicans' 
voter registration
 looked strong nationally. I couldn't find a transcript or clip with the word "collapsed." The claim also doesn't mention that his analysis was about polling swings and a Democratic edge in some races (
NYT/Siena had Talarico 51–45 over Paxton
), not a Republican collapse. Calling it a "collapse" is a stronger characterization than the sources support, and the Abbott link in the claim's context isn't backed by anything Enten said that I found. An emptywheel blog post does say Enten "ranted" about Abbott's redistrict

clusters.text: Democrats are favored to win Texas statewide for the first time in decades.
A Recon MR/Siena poll has Greg Abbott at 48% and Gina Hinojosa at 47%, Abbott up 3 points since September.
clusters.verdict_basis:
**Basis:** The ReconMR/Siena Texas Poll released October 13 has 
Governor: Abbott 48%, Hinojosa 47%, from Hinojosa 49–45% in September
. RealClearPolling lists the same poll, fielded 10/5–10/8 with 617 likely voters. It lists the September ReconMR/Siena poll (9/8–9/11) as 
45 for Abbott and 49 for Hinojosa
. So Abbott's own share rose from 45% to 48%, which is the 3 points the claim describes. Both toplines match.

The claim leaves out two things. The race went from Hinojosa +4 to Abbott +1, a five-point swing in the margin. 
The one-point difference is within the poll's margin of error, so the survey does not establish a clear leader
 (Newsweek). A reader could take "up 3 points" to mean Abbott's lead grew by 3, which would be wrong. As worded, though, it refers to his share, and that is accurate.

clusters.text: Greg Abbott is citing a scheduling conflict to skip the San Antonio rally with President Trump.
clusters.verdict_basis:
**1. Basis:** The claim is supported. 
Abbott's campaign confirmed to The Hill that he would skip the event. It pointed to his Monday remarks in Houston, where he said he had events scheduled that day in multiple cities and couldn't make it.
 
NBC News also reported that he cited a scheduling conflict.
 
Bloomberg reported that he would instead hold events in Jasper and College Station.
 
AP later confirmed he did not attend the rally.
 The claim describes the reason Abbott gave. Several outlets noted the political context of a tight race, but that doesn't change what he said. The claim also uses the present tense, which fit when it was first posted on Oct. 6, before the Oct. 7 rally.

clusters.text: A Fort Bend County public high school classroom has been turned into a Muslim Student Association 'mini-mosque' prayer hall.
clusters.verdict_basis: I found no report, district statement or official record of a Fort Bend County high school classroom being turned into an MSA "mini-mosque" prayer hall. The nearest recent matter is in Frisco ISD, which is in a different county. The RAIR Foundation and the Daily Signal reported that Liberty High School used a classroom for Muslim students to pray. Frisco ISD said the space is a "quiet room" that is not exclusive to one faith ([Heartlander/Daily Signal](https://heartlandernews.com/texas-high-school-faces-scrutiny-after-student-video-shows-muslims-only-prayer-room/); [RAIR](https://rairfoundation.com/exclusive-texas-high-school-turns-classroom-muslim-only/)). Fort Bend ISD pages show only ordinary MSA clubs that meet at campus sites. Examples are Bush High School in room C104 and Dulles High School in room A201, where meetings include prayers ([Bush HS MSA](https://www.fortbendisd.com/Page/25958); [Dulles HS MSA](https://www.fortbendisd.com/domain/1830)). A 2017 op-ed by a former student describes a long-standing practice at Fort Bend high schools of lending a sponsor's classroom for student prayer. That is an old first-person account, not evidence of a new conversion ([Religion News

clusters.text: Greg Abbott is America's governor.
A GBAO internal poll for Gina Hinojosa shows her at 47% and Greg Abbott at 45%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
**Basis:** The Hinojosa campaign's own press release says a new GBAO poll has 
Hinojosa leading Abbott 47% to 45% among likely voters
, and describes it as a poll from GBAO. Newsweek, in its Oct. 14 article on Ken Paxton's leaked remarks, also reports that 
a GBAO poll conducted for the Hinojosa campaign had her ahead 47 percent to 45 percent
. The claim's figures and attribution match. "Internal" is accurate because the campaign commissioned and released the poll. I did not find the GBAO memo itself, so the sample size and margin of error are unconfirmed. Other recent public polls show a mixed picture, but that doesn't affect this claim.

clusters.event: Oct 7 anniversary: Abbott orders flags to half-staff
clusters.text: A TSU poll of Fort Bend County has Gina Hinojosa leading Greg Abbott 51% to 40%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
**Basis:** The TSU Fort Bend County poll (October 2026) exists, but its numbers differ from the claim. The TSU PDF reports 
53% of likely voters for Hinojosa, 42% for Abbott, 2% for Libertarian Pat Dixon, and 3% undecided
. That is an 11-point lead. The claim says 51–40, which is also an 11-point gap. The Texan and TSU News both report the same 11-point margin. The claim's 51% and 40% do not match the published 53% and 42%. The 11-point gap is right, but the two figures the claim specifies are wrong.

clusters.event: Oct 7 anniversary: Abbott orders flags to half-staff
clusters.text: An Equis Research poll finds Gina Hinojosa leads Greg Abbott 59% to 35% among likely Latino voters.
clusters.verdict_basis:
**1. Basis:** I found no Equis Research poll of the Texas governor's race, and no report of a 59%–35% Latino split for Hinojosa over Abbott from Equis. The Latino numbers I did find come from other pollsters and differ from the claim. NBC5/Telemundo had 
Hinojosa up 13 points (52%-39%)
. YouGov had 
Hispanic voters at 58 percent to 37 percent
 for her. The Hinojosa campaign's release on the NYT/Siena poll had 
Latino voters (62-31%)
. The UT/Texas Politics Project poll had 
Hispanic voters preferring her 56-42
. The exact 59–35 figure appears in other contexts: 
non-white voters, 59-35%
 in NPR/Marist, and a South Texas/RGV regional result in NYT/Siena. This suggests the number may have been misattributed, but I can't confirm that. My searches were limited and may have missed an Equis release, so I can't verify the claim or rule it out. Checking Equis Research's own website or release page would settle it.

clusters.text: The TSU poll has James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 56% to 38% in Fort Bend County.
clusters.verdict_basis: **Basis:** The claim matches the poll as reported. The Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center at Texas Southern University surveyed 1,200 likely Fort Bend County voters. According to the poll summary quoted on Off the Kuff, 56% intend to vote for Talarico and 38% for Paxton, with 2% for Libertarian Ted Brown and 4% undecided . The Texan reports the same figures , and The Center Square also reports an 18-point Talarico lead in Fort Bend County . The sources differ slightly on field dates: September 29 to October 2, 2026 in the poll text, versus September 9 to October 2 in The Texan. The claim doesn't mention dates, so this doesn't affect it. The claim is a county-level poll, not a statewide one, and it says so. I did not find the TSU release itself, only reporting that quotes it.
